results.title: Trump Threatens to Raise EU Auto Tariffs to 25%
results.content: The Trump administration’s tariffs on imported vehicles and auto parts have cost automakers a staggering $35.4 billion since their implementation in 2025, according to an analysis of financial reports by Automotive News. Toyota has been the hardest hit, projecting $9.1 billion in tariff-related costs for the fiscal year ending March 2026. The three major Detroit automakers—General Motors, Ford, and Stellantis—collectively incurred $6.5 billion in costs in 2025, while other global brands like [...] The White House announced that passenger vehicles, certain trucks, and auto parts will be exempt from the new 10% global tariff set to take effect on February 24, 2026. This decision provides relief to automakers and dealers who were concerned about additional cost pressures, especially as the industry already faces significant expenses from existing tariffs on steel, aluminum, and imported auto parts. These sector-specific tariffs, implemented under national security grounds, remain unaffected [...] global brands like BMW, Honda, and Hyundai-Kia also reported significant financial impacts exceeding $1 billion each. These tariffs, which include a 15% tax on vehicles from the EU, Japan, and South Korea, as well as a 25% tariff on non-U.S. parts in North American vehicles, have disrupted the global supply chain and increased production costs.

results.title: Driving Up Costs? Trump's New 25% Tariff Hits Imported ...
results.content:
Share on:

The Trump administration has announced a 25% tariff on imported passenger vehicles and auto parts — on top of existing duties — potentially reshaping pricing, sourcing and production strategies across the auto industry. [...] It’s unclear whether these tariffs will revive domestic auto manufacturing — or simply drive up prices. Industry analysts forecast an increase in vehicle prices by $3,000 to $10,000. Many vehicles assembled in North America rely on global supply chains — a single car may include up to 20,000 parts from more than 50 countries.

### What This Means for Dealers, Manufacturers and Consumers [...] The tariff will apply to sedans, SUVs, crossovers, minivans, cargo vans and light trucks as well as key components including engines, transmissions, powertrain systems and electrical parts. According to Commerce Department data, the U.S. imported more than $400 billion in vehicles and auto parts in 2024 alone.
